7db510b3dbf2213c.title_original: Simply Logical -- The First Three Decades
7db510b3dbf2213c.summary: arXiv:2610.28912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper charts the evolution of the Prolog textbook Simply Logical -- Intelligent Reasoning by Example from print with runnable programmes on a 3.5-inch diskette published in 1994, via various intermediate online versions, to the fully interactive online edition available today. Our aim is to investigate -- from both the writer's and the reader's perspectives -- the potential impact of technology on educational materials. The three authors of this paper present three distinct and complementary points of view, which come together to shape an interactive online book that offers an immersive learning experience. Peter describes the philosophy behind the original book and experiences teaching from it. Jan demonstrates how contemporary web programming has enabled a fully interactive realisation of the book's philosophy. Kacper reports how different technologies can be adopted to build a versatile authoring toolkit that underpins the interactive online edition of the book. Collating these distinct yet coherent perspectives allows us to reflect on future opportunities for interactive Prolog teaching materials arising from the continuous development of web technologies. The insights we offer should be of interest to teachers of Prolog as well as those wanting to find out about the latest educational technologies.

5d9eff71c30023de.title: Same Answer, Different Reasons: Trace-Level Divergence in Multilingual Large Language Models
5d9eff71c30023de.title_original: Same Answer, Different Reasons: Trace-Level Divergence in Multilingual Large Language Models
5d9eff71c30023de.summary: arXiv:2610.29092v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multilingual large language models are increasingly deployed in settings where visible reasoning traces support verification, education, and safety auditing, yet standard evaluations typically measure only final-answer agreement or holistic response similarity. As a result, they establish outcome consistency without determining whether users across languages receive comparable supporting evidence. We introduce a trace-level divergence framework that compares visible reasoning traces as structured sequences, decomposing agreement into structural similarity, order consistency, and holistic similarity, with pair-specific calibration to enable comparison across languages. Across three reasoning benchmarks, seven languages, and six frontier LLMs, the natural baseline---embedding each whole response and comparing the two by cosine---systematically overstates agreement: $52.1\%$--$67.3\%$ of examples in the top quartile of holistic similarity are not in the top quartile of structural similarity. This dissociation is stable across sentence encoders and step segmentations, and blind bilingual annotation studies in two English-anchored language pairs show that human judgments align with structural similarity rather than with the holistic baseline. A same-language control shows that the level of divergence is language-specific: two English traces for paraphrases of the same question agree more closely than an English trace and its counterparts in other languages. Our results show that answer-level and holistic evaluations can substantially overestimate the consistency of multilingual explanatory artifacts, motivating trace-level evaluation for reliable multilingual deployment.

66c10e70f9806ad0.title: Compiling Autoregressive LLM Control into Policy-Exact Parallel Inference for Hierarchical RAG
66c10e70f9806ad0.title_original: Compiling Autoregressive LLM Control into Policy-Exact Parallel Inference for Hierarchical RAG
66c10e70f9806ad0.summary: arXiv:2610.30664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models increasingly act as controllers in structured decision pipelines, yet their decisions are still executed by autoregressive text decoding. Hierarchical RAG is one such setting: at each frontier of a document tree, an LLM commits to $b$ of $k$ sections under an input-dependent action grammar, executed as either failure-prone free-form JSON or reliable but strictly serial grammar-constrained generation. We show that this serialization is unnecessary for bounded-horizon control: the reachable future forms a shallow action-prefix tree, which we compile --- one root prefill plus one tree-causal probe evaluate every prefix-conditioned action distribution with serial decoding's tokens, positions, and causal ancestry. A prefix-state lemma makes compiled control policy-exact in exact arithmetic: the same policy with a two-forward critical path and zero output tokens. One further probe pass certifies the exact order-marginalized MAP set. Across four document-disjoint splits and two scales on the primary MetaX device, compiled control matches the serial policy on $84$--$89\%$ of questions --- every instrumented divergence a floating-point near-tie --- and cuts control latency by $35$--$47\%$ versus token-wise serial decoding and $6$--$7\%$ versus an idealized chunked engine; an H800 repetition preserves the ordering.

3c6ac20b4a4a1984.title: Learned Control Variates for Rare Grid-Outage Estimation at Electric Vehicle Charging Stations
3c6ac20b4a4a1984.title_original: Learned Control Variates for Rare Grid-Outage Estimation at Electric Vehicle Charging Stations
3c6ac20b4a4a1984.summary: arXiv:2610.27159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Public charging of electric vehicles (EVs) adds a large and synchronized load to the distribution feeders. In most networks, it is rare to overload a feeder at the same time. When it does happen, the consequences can be severe: an overloaded feeder stresses its transformers and can trigger cascading outages across a city. Planners who design for high reliability therefore need to estimate very small outage probabilities. To that end, plain Monte Carlo estimation with an expensive grid simulator can require a prohibitively large number of runs for this task. To reduce the number of runs, we propose a control variate (CV) built from a learned classifier of the outage, trained on cheap observable features such as temperature and load forecasts. We show that for any binary learner, the variance reduction is an explicit function of its recall and false-positive rate. Furthermore, we show that control variate based on a Gaussian proxy of the load loses its effect as outages become rarer, while a learner with non-vanishing precision keeps removing a fixed fraction of the variance even in the extreme rare-event regime. We verify these results in numerical experiments using a feeder-overload simulator across three orders of magnitude of outage probability and obtain that even weak learner with a single feature can remove a quarter of the variance, while a boosted-tree learner is able to remove about 60%. We then apply the estimator to the feeder network of Surabaya, Indonesia, in which the Gaussian load model leaves every feeder three to seven times the one-day-in-ten-years blackout target. At the same simulation budget, planning the reserve with the learned CV and a 95% confidence limit reduces the city-wide blackout days by a third compared with Monte Carlo. These results show that learned control variates can help planners design distribution grids that stay reliable against rare outages.

69e67b173b7b41c1.title: Extreme Low-State Quantized Transformer for Electricity-Load Forecasting
69e67b173b7b41c1.title_original: Extreme Low-State Quantized Transformer for Electricity-Load Forecasting
69e67b173b7b41c1.summary: arXiv:2610.28784v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Aggressive low-state weight quantization can substantially reduce neural-network representational flexibility, making predictive performance difficult to preserve when only a few discrete weight states are available. We investigate this regime for Transformer-based electricity-load forecasting using 3-, 5-, 7-, and 16-state weight quantization across feed-forward-only and attention-plus-feed-forward quantization. Two tasks predict either the next hour or the next 24 hours from the preceding 48 hours across two co-primary electricity-consumption datasets. Direct post-training quantization (PTQ) increased mean normalized root-mean-square error (NRMSE) relative to full precision by 6.25 and 7.04 percentage points in Datasets A and B, whereas quantization-aware fine-tuning (QAT-FT) recovered approximately 90.2% and 94.5% of these penalties. Quantization-aware training from random initialization (Scratch-QAT) also produced competitive low-state solutions, with particularly favorable behavior at three states. We further introduce accumulated-update thresholding, which accumulates optimizer-proposed weight changes before commitment. Relative to paired Scratch-QAT controls, this reduced committed shadow-weight updates by approximately 99.7% and discrete state transitions by approximately 77--80%, while mean NRMSE changed by only +0.042 and +0.197 percentage points. These results show that useful Transformer forecasting can be retained under highly discrete weight representations while strongly suppressing target-state activity, supporting a prospective route toward compact, low-activity edge forecasting using multilevel synaptic devices.

c67dc057ed7e7919.title: LightCRS: Lightweight Multi-Domain Conversational Recommendation System
c67dc057ed7e7919.title_original: LightCRS: Lightweight Multi-Domain Conversational Recommendation System
c67dc057ed7e7919.summary: arXiv:2610.26948v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conversational recommender systems have recently adopted vision-language models to match user dialogue intents with multimodal product information. However, extending these methods to many product domains faces a dilemma: deploying a separately adapted VLM per domain scales cost linearly with the number of domains and requires routing each dialogue to the right model, while naively merging all domains into a single VLM degrades accuracy because product characteristics vary widely across categories. We propose LightCRS, a lightweight, query-conditioned framework for unified multi-domain multimodal conversational recommendation. LightCRS precomputes multimodal product representations once offline with frozen encoders. Online, a compact 5.3M-parameter module fuses this evidence for each dialogue via query-conditioned cross-attention, whose parameters are shared across all domains, and compares candidates jointly with an inter-candidate Transformer. To enable rigorous evaluation, we construct MM-R2A-25, a 25-domain benchmark pairing natural Reddit recommendation-seeking conversations with Amazon product listings. LightCRS achieves state-of-the-art average HR@1, NDCG@5, and MRR, improving HR@1 by 35.4\% over the strongest baseline while reducing per-query latency by 266 times. Joint multi-domain training itself improves HR@1 by 15.2\% over separately trained single-domain models.

ba71c1a72cb63af0.title_original: MoSAIK: Motion Search with Artificial Intelligence in K-space
ba71c1a72cb63af0.summary: arXiv:2610.27156v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Object: Motion artefacts remain a major limitation of routine two-dimensional T2-weighted turbo spin-echo (TSE) brain MRI, reducing diagnostic confidence and often necessitating repeated acquisitions. MoSAIK (Motion Search with AI in K-space) retrospectively estimates in-plane rigid-body motion directly from standard multi-coil TSE k-space. Without a motion-free reference, external navigators, or additional acquisitions, MoSAIK infers motion from k-space self-consistency violations and incorporates predicted parameters into model-based, motion-aware reconstruction rather than synthesizing corrected images. Materials and Methods: Selected complex coil data were represented as log-magnitude and phase channels. A decoupled convolutional embedding and Transformer encoder estimated phase-encoding-line-indexed rotation and two-dimensional translations. Training used motion-free clinical acquisitions with simulated motion; four held-out subjects were evaluated. Component-wise errors assessed estimation; SSIM and PSNR in silico and entropy focus criterion (EFC) in vivo assessed reconstruction. Results: Motion estimation errors were low for both rotation (MSE $<$ 0.2 deg$^2$) and translation (MSE $<$ 0.2 pixels$^2$), with Pearson correlations of approximately 0.96 and 0.94, respectively. In every in-vivo acquisition, more than 75% of slices showed information gain relative to uncorrected reconstructions. MoSAIK reduced visible artefacts while preserving anatomical detail. Discussion: Transformer-based k-space motion-trajectory estimation enables fast retrospective correction of standard clinical TSE brain MRI.

5e0203280ad15f79.title: STAR-XPC: Set Transformer for Estimating X-ray Transmission in Polymer Composites
5e0203280ad15f79.title_original: STAR-XPC: Set Transformer for Estimating X-ray Transmission in Polymer Composites
5e0203280ad15f79.summary: arXiv:2610.28709v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evaluating the energy transmission ratio of an X-ray beam through a polymer composite is a challenging task in radiation shielding studies. The reference solution with Monte Carlo transport simulation is highly accurate but computationally expensive: each of our reference simulations is capped at $4\times10^9$ photon histories and a 20,000 s (over 5 hours) time limit, while closed-form analytical methods fail to represent such complex scenarios. We present an artificial neural network model that maps the unordered multi-set of molecular constituents, their mass fractions, and four bulk physical descriptors directly to the transmission ratio $I(t)/I_0$ in 1-3 milliseconds. The model is a Set Transformer, which makes it permutation invariant by construction and accepts mixtures of different sizes up to 11 constituents within a fixed-size padded set. Each constituent is embedded with a chemistry-pretrained transformer language model, ChemBERTa. In our proposed method, training data are produced by an automated PENELOPE/penEasy pipeline using the radiation source at 30, 80, 100, and 120 kV tube voltages over polyethylene-based shielding composite slabs of thicknesses spanning 0.15-2.5 mm. After preprocessing, the dataset contains $n = 4697$ simulated configurations on which a leakage-free, jointly stratified 10-fold cross-validation is performed, attaining mean squared error MSE = $(1.12 \pm 0.56)\times10^{-4}$, normalized-MSE percentage NMSE% = 0.0294% $\pm$ 0.0147%, and $R^2 = 0.9988$. The corresponding per-sample percentage errors give an alpha-trimmed ($\alpha = 0.10$) absolute percentage error (APE) of 1.66% and a median APE of 1.15%. Our model's inference is several orders of magnitude faster than the underlying Monte Carlo simulation (sub-millisecond per query vs. several hours for the reference run) with effective accuracy in predicting $I(t)/I_0$.

c6b23423c486408a.title: Big Claims, Small Margins: Do Reported GraphLLM Gains Survive Simple Baselines?
c6b23423c486408a.title_original: Big Claims, Small Margins: Do Reported GraphLLM Gains Survive Simple Baselines?
c6b23423c486408a.summary: arXiv:2610.28714v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-based methods for node classification on text-attributed graphs (TAGs) routinely report state-of-the-art accuracy. We ask how these results compare with inexpensive baselines run on the same splits. On the splits of three recent studies, we tune four baseline representatives with validation-only selection and compare them with the highest mean that each paper reports for an LLM-based method in the matched setting. Correct & Smooth on TF-IDF features trails this reference by a median of 2.3 percentage points, and an MLP on frozen e5-large-v2 embeddings by 2.8 points. Correct & Smooth is within 3 points of the reference or better on 15 of 24 tasks, but the reference is significantly higher on 12 of 22 testable tasks, so several reported gains remain substantial. Reading released code next to the papers, we also document evaluation risks: selection of hyperparameters or checkpoints on the test set, labels of test-pool nodes used in training, baseline numbers reused without disclosure, and a text-label misalignment in a released Cora loader. Reports of the same method on the same split also differ by up to 12.5 points across papers whose configurations are not documented to match.

6564e961d00a58a9.title: Dynamic System Inspired Continuous Large Language Model for AI4Science Tasks
6564e961d00a58a9.title_original: Dynamic System Inspired Continuous Large Language Model for AI4Science Tasks
6564e961d00a58a9.summary: arXiv:2610.26959v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific foundation models increasingly operate on continuous phenomena, yet still use discrete residual computation. We ask whether pretrained residual transformations can support additional latent computation without expanding the backbone. To test this possibility, we introduce Continuum-LM, which reuses these transformations as dynamical operators in a continuous-depth language model. Its hidden states evolve through an ordinary differential equation evaluated by higher-order numerical integration, with solver order and step size controlling computation. Across eight scientific tasks, Continuum-LM trains stably and improves mean exact-match accuracy by 7.77 and 10.96 percentage points over discrete counterparts at the 0.6B and 1.7B scales, respectively. At 0.6B, it also outperforms an Ouro-style recurrent control under matched parameter and residual-function evaluation budgets. Together, these results support extensible computational depth through parameter reuse, identifying continuous hidden-state evolution as a practical design dimension for scientific language models beyond parameter scaling.

3a9d7299ccc86fa3.title: Think Before You Transcribe: Context-Steered Reasoning for Hotword-Aware Speech Recognition
3a9d7299ccc86fa3.title_original: Think Before You Transcribe: Context-Steered Reasoning for Hotword-Aware Speech Recognition
3a9d7299ccc86fa3.summary: arXiv:2610.26986v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Contextual automatic speech recognition (ASR) improves rare-entity recognition by supplying candidate hotwords, but retrieved candidates may be incomplete or incorrect. A reliable system must therefore exploit a relevant candidate without allowing unsupported alternatives to override the acoustic evidence. We propose a context-steered reasoning framework that generates a short, audio-grounded caption before transcription. This task-specific representation lets the model assess candidate relevance before making a lexical decision. Supervised fine-tuning establishes the structured caption-to-transcription behavior, while targeted trajectory injection strengthens group relative policy optimization when difficult utterances yield only unsuccessful rollouts. Experiments across diverse context conditions show that the proposed method consistently improves both transcription quality and hotword recognition while remaining robust to irrelevant candidates.

ac83936e43caf9ca.title: ClockMark: Adaptive and Host-Dependent Watermarking for Large Language Models
ac83936e43caf9ca.title_original: ClockMark: Adaptive and Host-Dependent Watermarking for Large Language Models
ac83936e43caf9ca.summary: arXiv:2610.27079v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) watermarking operates on the next-token distribution that evolves during generation. In streaming generation, each sampled token becomes part of the text and affects subsequent distributions. Embedding therefore proceeds with a changing host, unlike classical watermarking, which adapts embedding to an existing host signal. To accommodate this difference, we formulate a novel embedding framework for LLM watermarking based on two principles. We first argue that embedding should be adaptive, retaining the state of previous sampling decisions to better guide subsequent choices. We further argue that embedding should be host-dependent, using the current LLM distribution to constrain both token selection and state updates. Guided by these principles and the two requirements of distribution preservation and robustness to text editing, we propose ClockMark. It combines adaptive and host-dependent embedding with message spreading, embedding the full payload in each watermarked token. Theoretically, we prove that ClockMark preserves the original LLM sequence distribution, thereby maintaining generation quality. Empirically, extensive experiments against 12 baselines demonstrate improved robustness to text editing, with gains of up to 16.08 percentage points in bit accuracy over the strongest tested baseline.

b1f6cb2a76b02a54.title: Cross-Lingual Reusability of LLM Pipelines: Financial Extraction, Multilingual Reasoning, and Semantic Screening
b1f6cb2a76b02a54.title_original: Cross-Lingual Reusability of LLM Pipelines: Financial Extraction, Multilingual Reasoning, and Semantic Screening
b1f6cb2a76b02a54.summary: arXiv:2610.27043v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Financial institutions increasingly deploy large language models (LLMs) in multilingual markets, raising a practical question: can pipelines developed and validated in English be reused across languages, or must they be rebuilt per locale? We test cross-lingual reusability along three dimensions--accuracy, reasoning-effort transfer, and behavioural stability--through three complementary tasks. Task 1 (cheque extraction) and Task 2 (Mintaka QA with pinned evidence across nine languages and nine model-effort configurations) test whether accuracy and effort settings transfer; Task 3 (FinanceBench pilot, 50 items over SEC 10-K filings in four languages) validates whether these patterns generalise to financial content. Accuracy reusability is broadly confirmed: Gemini 3.5 Flash achieves 95.2-97.6% extraction accuracy across prompt languages, and FinanceBench per-language means span 5.8pp (77.1-82.9%), though the language-difficulty ranking reverses between domains (Hindi is worst on Mintaka, best on FinanceBench at 82.9%). Effort reusability is domain-dependent: higher reasoning effort yields marginal gains on general-knowledge QA but up to 8pp on financial content, and effort configurations that help in English help proportionally in other languages. Behavioural reusability holds: citation-set overlap with English averages 77-79% Jaccard, with no single language consistently worse. Together, these results support qualified reuse of English-built pipelines, but per-domain, per-language validation remains necessary--neither semantic similarity nor self-reported confidence reliably predicts cross-lingual accuracy.

e9ca1d98a1a7f76f.title: A Theoretical Analysis of Environment-Aware Out-of-Distribution Detection for Vision-Language Models
e9ca1d98a1a7f76f.title_original: A Theoretical Analysis of Environment-Aware Out-of-Distribution Detection for Vision-Language Models
e9ca1d98a1a7f76f.summary: arXiv:2610.27211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Continual vision-language models (VLMs) encounter a stream of environments and must also reject inputs that do not belong to the environment at hand. Class information from earlier environments can aid out-of-distribution (OOD) detection, yet existing detectors score each environment in isolation, and when previous environments help or hurt is theoretically unclear. We develop a theory of environment-aware OOD detection built on contribution scores, pairwise cosine expectations measuring how the image and text features of one environment align with those of another. We propose a cross-environment maximum-concept-matching (MCM) score with two terms: a primary term matching the test image against the current class texts, and a secondary term matching it against the class texts of a previous environment, weighted by the intra-modal alignment between the two environments. We prove that, under a positive environment transition and a bounded class-matching margin for OOD inputs, this score attains a false-positive rate no larger than that of the standard MCM detector at an adjusted threshold. We then show that the score gap of an MCM detector between two environments equals the self-contribution of the in-distribution environment minus its cross-modal contribution into the OOD environment, which separates soft OOD environments, with explicit AUROC, true-positive, and false-positive guarantees, from hard ones, which no threshold that retains the in-distribution data can reliably reject. For cascaded detection, in which the text prototypes of all seen environments are pooled, the false-positive rate on every past environment is non-decreasing in time, and we characterize when detection provably fails. A contribution balance factor applied to the gradients of the classification loss and of a smoothed false-positive rate completes the framework.

9daf144c2c117269.title: CARAT: Do Materials LLMs Reason or Recite?
9daf144c2c117269.title_original: CARAT: Do Materials LLMs Reason or Recite?
9daf144c2c117269.summary: arXiv:2609.38340v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a materials LLM answers a question about crystal structure, does it reason from the structure or copy an answer already printed in its input? Accuracy cannot tell: a structural description often prints the very field it is scored against. CARAT holds question and gold answer fixed across eight matched views, names each structural relation separately in GraphSpace, and adds matched fine-tuning, answer masking, evidence injection, paired inference, and a rule that can withhold claims. First, on the benchmark's hardest families the grounded view is worth 17.3 points over formula inputs. Second, we turn that scrutiny on ourselves. GraphSpace beats a plain periodic graph by 19.3 points, but that margin is two effects at once: where the plain rendering carries everything the question needs it is 1.96 points, and where it omits those fields entirely, 46.7 points. The headline mostly measures what the baseline lacked, not how evidence is presented. Third, we attack our own benchmark. A rule that skips the link and reads the list directly answers four of seven hardened families, so we rebuilt it until eleven such shortcuts sat near chance. The frozen model quotes that link yet answers the same when we redirect it, on 95.6% of paired cases: it repeats the relation without using it. After matched supervision it reaches 99.8%, and deleting the link drops it to 23.4%, below the 27.0% the best shortcut reaches: both steps are learnable.

902b866af827e348.summary: IT之家 10 月 7 日消息，据彭博社报道，消息人士透露，AMD 首席执行官苏姿丰（Lisa Su）计划于周三与三星电子半导体业务负责人举行会晤，这是人工智能行业两位关键人物又一次面对面会谈。 知情人士称，苏姿丰在访问韩国期间，将会见负责三星核心芯片部门的副董事长全永铉（Jun Young‑hyun）。 当前各类存储产品普遍紧缺，给全球电子行业带来压力，也制约着 AI 基础设施与服务的扩张。存储芯片价格持续飙升，已经成为数据中心运营商最主要的成本项之一。早在今年 3 月，AMD 就已经和三星达成供货协议，合作方向包含新一代高带宽内存（HBM）以及先进存储芯片。 这是七个月之内苏姿丰第二次到访首尔。韩国在全球科技生态当中地位十分关键，既是 AI 硬件的重要供应方，同时也是重要消费市场。韩国正在统筹推动包括三星及本土同行 SK 海力士在内的企业，合计投入 8,800 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 5.91 万亿元人民币） ，用于面向 AI 时代的数字基础设施以及数据中心建设。 三星与 SK 海力士为全球多款高端 AI 加速芯片提供所必需的 HBM 高带宽内存。与此同时，韩国头部电信企业、制造厂商以及互联网平台公司，也都在大幅加码 AI 数据中心与下一代企业级服务领域的投资。

5e2b902bb7a35b76.summary: IT之家 10 月 6 日消息，据路透社上周（10 月 2 日）报道，亚马逊云计算（AWS）表示，未来 5 年将在全美国范围内的数据中心社区投资超 10 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 67.14 亿元人民币） ， 承诺为当地民众承担数据中心带来的水电资源影响 。 据报道，由于数据中心会对电力、公共事业成本等因素带来影响，美国各地民众近年来开始反对在自己的社区建设数据中心。随着美国 11 月 3 日中期选举临近，这种反弹态势给共和党带来了政治挑战。 亚马逊 AWS 表示，这笔超 10 亿美元的投资涵盖教育、职业培训、水资源和能源保护等领域。该公司试图回应数据中心耗电、环境等方面的负面影响，并称全美超 100 个数据中心项目已在考虑暂停建设。 此外亚马逊承诺， 到 2030 年 ， 公司所有数据中心将实现“水资源正效益”（water positive） ，即向社区返还的水资源多于数据中心自身消耗的水资源。该公司表示，该目标当前已完成 75%。

5ede9b4034fa199a.title: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra 破解拿破仑 1809 年密信，揭示 217 年前军事部署
5ede9b4034fa199a.title_original: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra 破解拿破仑 1809 年密信，揭示 217 年前军事部署
5ede9b4034fa199a.summary: IT之家 10 月 4 日消息，一名 AI 研究人员借助 OpenAI GPT-6 Astra 成功破解了一封拿破仑 · 波拿巴写于 1809 年的加密军事信件。这封信此前因密码本遗失，在过去 217 年里始终未能被完整解读。 该破解工作由 SentinelOne 员工、AI 工程师卡特 · 丘奇（Carter Church）完成。他表示，他使用 GPT-6 Astra 模型，从一张历史文献扫描图像开始，对信件进行文字识别和密码分析，整个过程约耗时 6 小时。 这封信写于 1809 年 3 月 16 日，当时奥地利正准备对法国开战。拿破仑致信自己的继子、意大利总督欧仁 · 德 · 博阿尔内（Eugène de Beauharnais），要求其通过加密信件向法国将领奥古斯特 · 德 · 马尔蒙（Auguste de Marmont）传递军事信息。现存文件开头包含一行普通法语，随后则是 24 行由数字、字母及自创符号组成的加密文本。 研究人员此前已经确认了其中 33 个符号的含义，但由于完整密码本丢失，其余部分一直无法破解。IT之家注意到，该信件包含约 1300 个密码单元和 155 种不同符号，其中部分符号代表单个字母，部分符号则对应完整法语单词。 Church 介绍，GPT-6 Astra 首先分析扫描图像，将文档切分为多个区域并识别其中的符号，随后尝试破解密码结构。模型采用了模拟退火算法等方法，对不同符号可能对应的字母和单词组合进行大量测试，并结合历史法语文本中的字母和词语规律进行比对。 在分析过程中，AI 参考了包括大仲马、维克多 · 雨果以及马尔蒙本人相关作品在内的历史法语文本特征，以评估不同破解结果的合理性。同时，模型还发现部分符号并不代表单独字母，而是对应完整法语词汇。 破解后的内容揭示了拿破仑在 1809 年奥地利战争爆发前夕的军事部署信息。信件列出了法国及盟军在欧洲多个地区的兵力情况，包括巴伐利亚、波兰、萨克森和意大利方向的军队，以及向奥地利推进的俄罗斯军队情况。 该解密结果还补充了部分此前历史记录中缺失的信息。研究显示，这封写给马尔蒙的信件包含有关奥地利军队部署、马尔蒙所处位置以及法国方面军事计划的更多细节。马尔蒙当时驻扎在达尔马提亚地区，远离拿破仑主要军队，因此拿破仑希望通过这封信让其了解整体战局并做好行动准备。 Church 表示，这类破解工作理论上也可以由人工完成，但通常需要大量时间和专业知识。此次 AI 系统的特点在于，它能够同时完成历史文档识别、符号分类、密码推理以及文本重建等此前通常由不同领域专家分别完成的任务，而且只用了 6 个小时。 为验证模型并非依赖已有历史资料直接生成答案，Church 还重新运行了分析流程，并移除了与拿破仑和马尔蒙相关的历史文本作为参考。据其介绍，模型仍然得到了相同的解读结果。此次破解结果随后得到历史密码研究数据库 Cryptiana 维护者 Satoshi Tomokiyo 的认可，该数据库已将马尔蒙信件标记为已破解密码。

f048b82482d87c4a.title: 特斯拉 FSD 将迎重要升级：可避路面坑洼，导航学习用户驾驶习惯
f048b82482d87c4a.title_original: 特斯拉 FSD 将迎重要升级：可避路面坑洼，导航学习用户驾驶习惯
f048b82482d87c4a.summary: IT之家 10 月 4 日消息，特斯拉的 FSD（监督版）今年取得了长足进展：业务向欧洲市场拓展，商用无人驾驶 Robotaxi 也正式落地。不过即便是忠实使用者也清楚，这套系统依旧存在若干长期未能解决的短板。车主反馈最多的两大痛点集中在路线规划与破损路面问题：导航会莫名其妙绕路；FSD 还会径直开过容易扎破轮胎的坑洼路面。 好在这两大问题很快就有望得到修复。Shopify 高管法尔汉 · 塔瓦尔（Farhan Thawar）在 X 平台发帖称赞 FSD v14.3.10 版本，同时也提到破损的沥青路面以及顽固的导航选路逻辑仍是他使用过程当中最大的困扰。 特斯拉 AI 团队首席软件工程师菲尔 · 段（Phil Duan）直接对此作出回复，确认“针对这两方面的改进即将上线。” IT之家注意到，自动避让路面坑洼是用户呼声最高的功能之一，特斯拉自 2019 年起就已经对此作出过承诺。近期埃隆 · 马斯克也表示坑洼避让功能很快就会正式推出；自今年春季 FSD v14.3 版本开始，特斯拉更是已经在版本更新说明中将该项功能列为待上线改进项。 现阶段的版本偶尔已经可以观察到类似效果。一名测试人员使用 FSD v14.2.2.5 时录下一段视频：车辆行驶时会微调位置，让开裂的路面坑洼刚好处于两侧车轮之间安全通过。但目前尚无法确认神经网络究竟是识别出了坑洼，还只是对一处无法判定的路面异常做出反应；并且该行为在近期各个 FSD 版本当中表现并不稳定。 一旦特斯拉正式推出坑洼避让，这种偶尔出现的避险动作就会转变为稳定可靠的行驶逻辑。以后不再需要驾驶员手动接管来保护轮毂、保障乘坐舒适性，FSD 可以实时识别破损路面，平稳转向绕开坑洼。 导航逻辑同样会迎来大规模重构。虽然 FSD 处理变道、转向的表现尚可，但车主经常吐槽整体选路逻辑：系统总是固执地选择奇怪的支路绕行，而不是沿用车主日常通勤习惯的路线。 特斯拉的解决思路是让 FSD 学习用户的日常驾驶习惯。系统分析驾驶员人工介入的操作，把用户手动选择车道、轻打方向盘的操作当作训练反馈。如果你总是无视导航规划的绕行路线，坚持走自己偏好的高速出口或者城市地面道路，后续出行时 FSD 就会记住这一偏好，不再和驾驶者“较劲抢方向盘”。该新功能建立在特斯拉此前上线的「偏好路线」（Preferred Routes）特性的基础之上。 除此之外，这套学习机制还会延伸至终点停车环节。后续版本的 FSD 将会学习你的停车习惯：记录你是习惯倒车驶入自家车道、紧贴车库墙体留出人行空间，还是停车时与高大路沿保持更远距离。完成学习之后，车辆在自动泊车时就会尽量模仿这些个人习惯。 除坑洼感知与更智能的路线规划以外，特斯拉还正在把 Grok 直接整合进 FSD 的整套系统。驾驶员不再需要点击屏幕菜单；很快就可以使用自然语音直接下达自动驾驶指令，例如要求车辆在某个路口转弯、停放到指定位置，或是临时更改行驶路线。再加上已经上线的自动避险功能 —— 该功能可以在人工驾驶状态下重新激活 FSD 辅助避险。看得出来，特斯拉当下正在紧锣密鼓迭代 FSD。 坑洼避让最初写进了 v14.3 版本更新说明当中，但目前尚不清楚这项升级究竟会随近期的小版本补丁推送，还是等到 FSD v15 架构才正式亮相。FSD v15 预计会带来一次重大神经网络升级，参数量达到 100 亿。无论上线节奏如何，让车辆学会避让路面坑洼、记住车主偏爱的通行道路，都将会让日常自动驾驶通勤的体验顺滑不少。

632792c5c6b5053b.title_original: 神舟二十三号乘组太空过双节：开展人在多任务状态下的大脑与人机适配研究
632792c5c6b5053b.summary: IT之家 10 月 4 日消息，据央视新闻报道，国庆假期，太空出差三人组 —— 神二十三乘组航天员朱杨柱、张志远、黎家盈仍在中国空间站值守。 三名航天员在轨驻留已四月有余，中秋国庆期间，他们将站内环境布置得温馨喜庆，同时，空间科学实（试）验、空间站组合体平台照料、健康管理等各项工作有序推进。 乘组使用太空拉曼光谱仪对尿液样本中的代谢组分进行检测，开展菌群与营养代谢研究，并按计划开展人在多任务状态下的大脑与人机适配研究。 测试数据用于揭示航天特殊环境对航天员认知控制的影响规律、脑功能机制及其认知计算原理 ，同时调整舱内灯光进行绩效测试，探究光环境对心理感知与工作效率的影响。 在微重力物理科学领域，乘组完成了在线维修装调操作柜内惯性粒子实验模块安装、流体物理实验柜内样品更换、轴心机构电极维护等。此外，乘组对生命生态实验柜进行在轨维护，更换了湿度控制单元模块。 IT之家获悉，在空间站组合体平台照料方面，乘组完成再生生保系统设备检查维护，按计划更换了相关组件，对舱内环境进行了定期清洁。 在健康管理方面，三名航天员完成颈部超声检查、骨密度测量、眼压及眼底检查、质量测量等多项医学检查，并使用中医四诊仪进行诊疗，持续监测在轨身体状态。

5caa930ce9f79d61.title_original: SK 海力士重申：尚未决定 Solidigm 未来资本利用规划
5caa930ce9f79d61.summary: IT之家 10 月 1 日消息，SK 海力士 (SK hynix) 韩国当地时间今日进一步澄清，重申旗下企业级固态硬盘企业 Solidigm （思得）仍在就增强竞争力的各项可能举措进行评估， 截至目前尚未做出任何决定 。 Solidigm 正积极提升自身业务竞争力。公司会持续评估投资需求，以确保产能和技术竞争力，并充分考虑市场和商业环境的变化。有关 Solidigm 的资本利用计划 需要综合考虑公司的整体投资计划、财务状况和资本配置进行审查 。 SK 海力士目前财务状况稳健，支持多样化的资金利用方案。是否使用外部资本需要考虑其对现有股东经济价值的影响，资本部署的总体有效性和融资的财务影响也是评估事项。 SK 海力士将 以企业和股东长期价值作为任何选项的首要标准 。如果未来确定具体计划，董事会将彻底评估其财务和运营影响，并忠实遵守所有相关法规和程序。

127be79366c3efd1.title_original: 新思科技与亚马逊签署多年期超 10 亿美元协议，推进定制芯片合作
127be79366c3efd1.summary: IT之家 9 月 30 日消息，当地时间 9 月 30 日，新思科技宣布与亚马逊达成多年期定制芯片 IP 战略合作协议，合作范围进一步拓展至云端及 AI 赋能的工程研发领域。 官方表示，通过引入新思科技的芯片知识产权以及 AI 驱动的工程软件解决方案，将加速亚马逊定制芯片与 AWS 基础设施的工程研发进程。 双方达成 多年期、总额超 10 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 67.18 亿元人民币） 的合作协议，新思科技将借助 AWS 服务加快自身产品迭代步伐，并与亚马逊协同针对 Trainium 与 Graviton 芯片深度优化新思科技旗下的软件工具。 此外，新思科技工程团队还将全面引入亚马逊弹性计算云（Amazon EC2）与 Amazon Bedrock，以此加速其前沿产品的开发效率。

44b33aaf227e6a09.title: 极氪：没有开发换电车型的规划，聚焦超快充与电混
44b33aaf227e6a09.title_original: 极氪：没有开发换电车型的规划，聚焦超快充与电混
44b33aaf227e6a09.summary: IT之家 9 月 30 日消息， 在吉利控股集团与蔚来公司达成充换电领域战略合作后 ，市场开始关注极氪是否会顺势开发换电车型。对此，极氪方面 9 月 29 日晚给出明确回应： 极氪没有开发换电车型的规划 。 极氪表示， 未来的产品路线仍将聚焦两大方向 ：一是具备超快充能力的纯电车型，二是行业首创的浩瀚超级电混车型，通过极致的补能技术与产品体验，为用户带来科技豪华出行体验。 极氪表示，在纯电方向上，极氪拥有目前业内领先的全栈 900V 高压架构，具备充电更快、性能更强、能耗更低的特点。以纯电车型焕新极氪 001 为例，电量从 10% 充到 70% 的平均时间只需 4 分 30 秒，刷新了全球量产车充电最快的纪录。 官方注释称，这一成绩来自搭载 95 度神盾金砖电池的焕新极氪 001 在吉利智充站使用极速充的平均充电时间； 该功能将率先在焕新极氪 001 上推送，后续通过 OTA 推送实现 。 在超级电混方向上，极氪 9X 满油满电的最大综合续航达 1250 公里，纯电续航最长可达 380 公里，电量从 20% 充到 80% 最快仅需 9 分钟。 极氪表示，将继续加大投入，持续提升用户在多场景下的补能效率。 据IT之家 9 月 28 日报道，蔚来集团与吉利控股集团正式达成充换电领域的全面战略合作，双方达成技术、运营、资本全方面合作共识， 将联合投资双方充换电业务主体公司，共享充换电技术与标准，共建充换电服务网络 。 根据双方达成的协议： 吉利控股集团将以其持有的易易互联 100% 股权及现金 6.4 亿元入股蔚来能源，交易完成后，吉利控股集团将持有蔚来能源 30% 股权，易易互联营运车辆换电业务将并入蔚来能源，蔚来能源将持续提升营运车辆换电网络的运营，赋能易易互联营运车辆业务； 双方将共建统一的 C 端换电技术和标准， 吉利控股集团将开发面向 C 端的换电车型 ，蔚来能源将为吉利控股集团 C 端换电车型提供服务。

1fe7fc25411a344a.title: 报告：美国人开始问 AI“吃什么零食”，高蛋白和重口味食品需求增长
1fe7fc25411a344a.title_original: 报告：美国人开始问 AI“吃什么零食”，高蛋白和重口味食品需求增长
1fe7fc25411a344a.summary: IT之家 9 月 23 日消息，据路透社报道，康尼格拉食品公司（Conagra Brands）称，越来越多美国消费者开始向人工智能询问“该吃什么零食”。这家 Slim Jim 肉类零食棒制造商表示，这一消费习惯正在推动高蛋白食品、浓郁风味产品以及针对特定健康目标定制的食品需求增长。 受减肥药快速普及以及白宫“让美国再次健康”（Make America Healthy Again）倡议等因素影响，美国消费者对更健康食品的需求比以往任何时候都更加旺盛。 康尼格拉食品同时也是亨氏（Hunt's）番茄酱的生产商。该公司与市场研究机构 Circana 合作，分析了美国零食市场超过 5300 万笔购物交易，覆盖约 1.7 万种产品。美国零食行业每年的零售销售额达到 1,982 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 1.33 万亿元人民币） ，其增长速度约为整个食品市场的 1.4 倍。 康尼格拉食品负责增长科学业务的高级副总裁鲍勃 · 诺兰（Bob Nolan）表示，自新冠疫情以来的 6 年时间里，美国人的饮食和食品消费方式发生的变化，比此前 50 年还要多。 诺兰周三表示：“无论消费者是希望补充蛋白质、获得更持久的能量，还是单纯享受片刻令人感到舒适的放纵，零食都正在消费者生活中扮演越来越重要、也越来越个性化的角色。” 不过，健康趋势只是其中一个因素。康尼格拉食品的研究发现，年轻消费者，尤其是 Z 世代，正在推动消费者对更大胆口味的需求，从甜辣组合，到酸爽、咸鲜等口味的零食，市场偏好都在发生变化。 康尼格拉食品表示，消费者也开始更加仔细地审视食品配料，并越来越多地使用 AI 工具来辅助购买决策。与其直接搜索某一种具体产品，消费者现在更倾向于告诉 AI 自己的需求，例如寻找蛋白质含量或膳食纤维含量更高的零食。 诺兰表示：“这就是为什么一些传统品类一直承受压力。”他指出，饼干和咸味零食等品类的表现一直较为疲软。 诺兰表示：“这些营养密度更高的零食，以及以特定目的为导向的零食消费方式，已经开始真正实现增长，并且正在加速。”

dbeadc05f95cc3fa.title: Evaluating Whether LLMs Can Reliably Connect the DOTs?
dbeadc05f95cc3fa.title_original: Evaluating Whether LLMs Can Reliably Connect the DOTs?
dbeadc05f95cc3fa.summary: arXiv:2609.38406v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Access to real-world information is often noisy and fragmented. Constructing a coherent narrative from such fragments requires models to reconstruct missing spans within a broader storyline, commonly referred to as text infilling, while preserving consistency with both the local context and the global storyline. Despite using text infilling as a pre-training objective in many Large Language Models (LLMs), their actual performance on real-world narrative infilling remains underexplored. In this paper, we address this gap by introducing a multi-domain benchmark of ~9.2K instances for narrative infilling, constructed by masking one to three sentences across four narrative types: encyclopedic text, commonsense stories, news articles, and visual narratives. Using this benchmark, we evaluate 20 instruction-tuned open-source LLMs ranging from 1.5B to 70B parameters across varying levels of instruction specificity and reasoning guidance. Outputs are assessed using standard automatic metrics and a qualitative framework covering five narrative dimensions. Results show that model scale does not reliably predict infilling quality: Gemma-2-2B achieves the highest qualitative score (4.02/5), outperforming models over ten times larger, including DeepSeek-Qwen-32B (3.77/5, 6.6%) and LLaMA-3.3-70B (3.71/5, 8.3%). We further find that explicit reasoning offers limited benefits as chain-of-thought reasoning yields only a marginal improvement (+0.6%). Additionally, short narratives and domain characteristics emerge as stronger predictors of task difficulty than infill position alone for narrative infilling in current LLMs.

d5018d9fbc466c37.title: NAQD Env: A benchmark for selective withdrawal in language agents
d5018d9fbc466c37.title_original: NAQD Env: A benchmark for selective withdrawal in language agents
d5018d9fbc466c37.summary: arXiv:2609.38460v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language agents must revise planned actions when evidence changes, permission is revoked, or a stop instruction arrives. A useful response is selective: suspend affected actions, preserve unaffected work, and resume only after sufficient repair. We introduce NAQD-Env, a synthetic environment that evaluates these decisions against a deterministic reference policy over explicit evidence, authorization, and constraint dependencies. Eleven dependency families support evaluation on development structures, held-out families, and held-out combinations of structures. Metrics distinguish attempted violations from violations permitted by a simulated execution gate and jointly report policy agreement, task value, withdrawal, resumption, and event reporting. We evaluate three open-weight instruction-tuned models from two families under three prompt conditions on 350 frozen scenarios, yielding 3,150 model-prompt episodes before gate replay. Across the reported conditions, withdrawal recall is at most 0.06, no valid resumption is observed at eligible opportunities, and only one episode matches the complete reference policy. Under the NAQD prompt, Qwen2.5-7B has fewer unsafe-attempt episodes than Qwen2.5-3B and Llama-3.1-8B, but also completes less useful work and preserves unaffected actions less accurately. Exploratory supervised fine-tuning probes increase Qwen2.5-3B decision accuracy from 0.45-0.54 to 0.83-0.92; separate diagnostics reveal inappropriate withdrawal after curriculum omissions and a loss of event reporting. These results motivate evaluating selective withdrawal as a distinct component of agent reliability. The setting measures policy application with trusted structured inputs and does not establish real-world containment or source-verification ability.
